contribution_requirements_justification: https://github.com/mmcintosh/better-auth-id-jag/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md — the requirements for acceptable contributions: tests with every change (a bug fix includes the test that would have caught it), security checks added to the mutation lists, docs updated with the code, a CHANGELOG entry, a DECISIONS.md entry for design choices, Biome lint with --error-on-warnings and TypeScript strict as the coding standard; pnpm typecheck, lint, docs:check, test and pack:check must pass. CI runs these on every pull request.
license_location_justification: Non-trivial license location file in repository: <https://github.com/mmcintosh/better-auth-id-jag/blob/main/LICENSE>.
floss_license_justification: The MIT license is approved by the Open Source Initiative (OSI).
floss_license_osi_justification: The MIT license is approved by the Open Source Initiative (OSI).
documentation_basics_justification: Some documentation basics file contents found.
repo_public_justification: Repository on GitHub, which provides public git repositories with URLs.
repo_track_justification: Repository on GitHub, which uses git. git can track the changes, who made them, and when they were made.
repo_interim_justification: The repository holds every interim version between releases, not only releases: https://github.com/mmcintosh/better-auth-id-jag/commits/main
repo_distributed_justification: Repository on GitHub, which uses git. git is distributed.
version_unique_justification: Each release has a unique semantic version number in package.json, published once to npm (npm refuses to reuse a version) and tagged in git: https://www.npmjs.com/package/better-auth-id-jag?activeTab=versions and https://github.com/mmcintosh/better-auth-id-jag/tags
version_semver_justification: Semantic Versioning: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH, with what each part promises while the IETF draft moves documented in https://github.com/mmcintosh/better-auth-id-jag/blob/main/docs/versioning.md
version_tags_justification: Every release is a git tag vX.Y.Z on main, created by the tag-release workflow when the release pull request merges; the release workflow refuses a tag that doesn't match package.json or isn't on main: https://github.com/mmcintosh/better-auth-id-jag/tags
release_notes_justification: Non-trivial release notes file in repository: <https://github.com/mmcintosh/better-auth-id-jag/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md>.
release_notes_vulns_justification: A release that fixes a vulnerability says so in a Security section of the CHANGELOG; advisories go through GitHub security advisories with CVEs where one applies (SECURITY.md)
report_process_justification: Non-trivial SECURITY[.md] file found file in repository: <https://github.com/mmcintosh/better-auth-id-jag/blob/main/SECURITY.md>. [osps_do_02_01]
report_responses_justification: The maintainer responds to issues; SECURITY.md sets a 7-day acknowledgement target for vulnerability reports
enhancement_responses_justification: Feature requests through the feature form; the README's "Not yet" section and the CHANGELOG record decisions
report_archive_justification:
GitHub issues and pull requests are public, permanently archived and searchable: 
  https://github.com/mmcintosh/better-auth-id-jag/issues?q=is%3Aissue
build_justification: `pnpm build` (scripts/build.mjs); CI builds and packs on every change
test_justification: `pnpm test` (Vitest) on Node and on workerd with D1; documented in CONTRIBUTING
test_most_justification: About 870 test runs, 436 each on Node (node:sqlite) and workerd (D1): unit, integration through real Better Auth hosts, property-based fuzzing, concurrency, interop with Keycloak and node-oauth2-server, a cross-repository SAML end-to-end test, and an adapter matrix on Postgres, MySQL and MongoDB including Prisma and Drizzle. The built package is checked under strict TypeScript 7 and 5.9.
test_policy_justification: CONTRIBUTING: "Tests with every change. A bug fix comes with the test that would have caught it."
tests_are_added_justification: CONTRIBUTING: "Tests with every change. A bug fix comes with the test that would have caught it."
tests_documented_added_justification: Every DECISIONS entry lists its tests; every security check is in a mutation list (test/mutations/*.json), broken once and caught by a test, weekly in CI (e.g. D-022, D-025)
warnings_justification: TypeScript `strict`, Biome lint with `--error-on-warnings` in CI
warnings_fixed_justification: CI fails on lint warnings and type errors
know_secure_design_justification: docs/security.md (the threats and controls, and the known limitations); the design reviews and an external pre-release review recorded in DECISIONS (D-007, D-014, D-015, D-022, D-025)
know_common_errors_justification: Token replay (single use by a unique key), audience and token-type confusion (exact aud, typ oauth-id-jag+jwt), algorithm confusion (no HS*/none), SSRF and slow responses when fetching keys, account takeover through email matching, information leaks in errors, and log injection are addressed and tested (docs/security.md)
crypto_published_justification: JWS signatures with RS256, ES256 and EdDSA (RFC 7515, 7518, 8037); SHA-256 for replay keys: published, standard algorithms
crypto_call_justification: jose and the platform's WebCrypto; no custom cryptographic primitives
crypto_floss_justification: All cryptography is implementable with FLOSS
crypto_keylength_justification: The package generates no long-term keys: ID-JAGs are signed with Better Auth's jwt plugin keys (EdDSA by default; ES256 or RS256, RSA at least 2048 bits, configurable). The receiver uses only RS256, ES256 and EdDSA keys from configured issuers.
crypto_working_justification: Only RS256, ES256 and EdDSA are accepted; HS* and none are refused, and an issuer's accepted algorithms are narrowed to those its key set publishes
crypto_pfs_justification: The plugin doesn't implement network protocols; TLS is the host's
crypto_password_storage_justification: The plugin stores no passwords; Better Auth does
crypto_random_justification: Identifiers (jti) and test keys from WebCrypto (`crypto.getRandomValues`); tokens and keys from Better Auth
delivery_unsigned_justification: No hash is retrieved over HTTP
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: No publicly known unpatched vulnerabilities; OSV-Scanner over every lockfile reports none (advisories without an update, all outside the published package, are recorded with reasons and an expiry in `osv-scanner.toml`)
static_analysis_justification: CodeQL (security-extended) on every pull request and push to `main`, and weekly; Biome; TypeScript strict
static_analysis_fixed_justification: CodeQL alerts are fixed or dismissed with a recorded reason (D-026: two fixed in the package, the rest in scripts and demos dismissed with the reason)
dynamic_analysis_justification: Property-based fuzzing (fast-check) of the ID-JAG parser, the issuer's request handling and the SAML token decoder on every CI run; mutation testing of every security check weekly
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: Fuzzing findings were fixed (D-007: a header whose toString throws)
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: GitHub Actions on every pull request and every push to main (.github/workflows/ci.yml): tests on both runtimes and two Better Auth versions, the adapter matrix, the built package, the example Workers, gitleaks; plus CodeQL, dependency audits and review, OSV-Scanner and OpenSSF Scorecard.
discussion_justification: GitHub supports discussions on issues and pull requests.
no_leaked_credentials_justification: gitleaks scans the full history in CI; test keys are generated per run
